props.gloss_en: the mishnah: a tumtum and an androginos -- neither in the Temple nor in the country
R' Yishmael: you have no blemish greater than this
the Sages: it is not a firstborn
Abaye: cracked is like broken -- as broken is in a place of bone, so cracked is in a place of bone
Rava: even without 'broken', a crack in a place of flesh is not a blemish
the stam, for R' Yishmael: perhaps [Rava's rule holds] where it is not noticeable; but where it is noticeable we call it 'an ill blemish'
(horn 1) it is obvious to R' Yishmael that the androginos is a firstborn and its blemish is with it
(horn 2) or R' Yishmael is in doubt and speaks 'if you should say': if you should say it is a firstborn, its blemish is with it
the stam: what is the practical difference? to flog on its account for shearing and for work
the stam: or alternatively, to give it to a priest
R' Ilai in R' Yishmael's name: an androginos is a firstborn, and its blemish is with it
the baraita: 'a male' -- and not a female; when it says 'a male' below, which is unneeded, why does it say it? to exclude a tumtum and an androginos
the stam: does a verse come to exclude a doubt? (rhetorical: it does not -- used at 41b.5 and again at 41b.7)
the baraita is the first tanna's
the baraita is the later Rabbis' (the Sages of the mishnah)
rather, it is obviously R' Yishmael's
the stam: and of the firstborn two verses are written: 'the male' and 'the males'

questions.gloss_en: Rava: what is R' Yishmael's reason -- is it obvious to him that the androginos is a firstborn with its blemish (p_ry_pashit), or is he in doubt and speaks 'if you should say' (p_ry_mesupak)? Both ta-shemas (41b.3, 41b.4) are deflected; no resolution or teiku
